blocks.text: Uthmaan (RA). She says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) never awakened any members of the household (at night when he awoke for Tahajjud). The only time he would ask any of them to get him water for wudhu was if he found them awake. He also fasted perpetually."[^1]
Hadhrat Hasan says, "I saw Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sleeping in the Masjid covered in a shawl. Although he was then the Ameerul Mu'mineen, there was none around him."[^2]
The Humility of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

Hadhrat Unaysa says, "The little girls of the locality would take their goats to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) (for milking). (Not only would he do it for them but) He would also ask, 'Would you like me to milk for you like Ibn Afraa (someone from the Ansaar) does?'"[^3]

The narrations of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA), Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Ibn Musayyab have already passed in the chapter entitled "The Lives of the Khulafaa and Leaders". It is stated there[^4] that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) was a businessman by trade and would proceed to the marketplace every morning to buy and sell. He also had a flock of goats that would come to him in the evenings. He sometimes took them out himself for grazing and sometimes had someone else graze them. He used to milk goats for the people of his locality so when he became the Khalifah, a little girl said, "Now there will be none to milk our animals." When he heard her saying this, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Why not! I swear by my life that I shall definitely still milk for you. I hope that what I have entered into will never change the personality I always had." He then continued milking for the people and would sometimes say to the little girl of the locality, "Dear girl! Would you like me to make the milk foamy or without foam?" At times she would ask for foamy milk while at times she asked for it to have no foam. He then did exactly as she asked.
Episodes of the Humility of Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Ali (RA)

The blanket merchant Hadhrat Saalih reports from his grandfather who says, "I saw (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ali (RA) purchase dates for a Dirham and then carry them in his bag. When I or another man offered to carry it for him, he refused the offer saying, 'The father of a family has a greater right to carry their goods.'"[^5]
Hadhrat Zaadhaan reports that even as Ameerul Mu'mineen, Hadhrat Ali (RA) used to walk alone in the marketplace where he would guide lost people,
